::: {.why}
Six or seven classic signals evaluated identically on one universe with one cost model is a comparison almost nobody publishes, and it is the most defensible page in milestone 6.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Rank every signal by net information ratio with intervals, and state which are distinguishable from the null.
- State the total number of specifications tried across the week and the correction that implies.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>65 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [30 min]{.task-min} Produce the comparison table: every signal with rationale, IC, decay horizon, gross and net information ratio with intervals, turnover, capacity and its position in the null distribution. One table, one page, sorted by net.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [25 min]{.task-min} Apply the correction to the set rather than to each signal: read the trial count from research_log.jsonl for the whole week, compute the threshold from qlib/noise.py at that count, and mark which signals clear it. Then keep the ones that do not in the table, with the diagnosis. A book with only winners in it is a book that was filtered.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [10 min]{.task-min} Write the paragraph on decay: for each signal, note its publication date and whether your post-publication estimate is lower, and connect that to what McLean and Pontiff report.
:::
:::
